answer: A work-bonded registry resists sybils: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed on fraud, and new identities earn trust only through a slow, verifiable history of useful work. A gale of fresh accounts then costs real money to plant, while a velvet-gloved reputation score quietly gates high-value jobs behind proven behavior. Like tending a garden, honest agents grow privileges season by season, so an attacker must fund many long-lived identities instead of spawning thousands for free.
